title: Baked Mac and Cheese
seoTitle: Baked Mac and Cheese | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac
description: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Salt the pasta water
steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with enough salt that it tastes like the sea. This is your only chance to season the pasta itself.

steps.title: Cook sauce base
steps.instruction: Meanwhile, brown meat, add onions and garlic, then tomatoes (and cream if Alfredo-style). Simmer 15 minutes while pasta cooks.

steps.title: Boil pasta al dente
steps.instruction: Cook pasta 1 minute shy of package time. Reserve 2 cups pasta water. Drain — do not rinse.

steps.title: Finish in the pan
steps.instruction: Toss pasta in sauce over medium heat, splashing pasta water until glossy and clinging. Baked Mac and Cheese should coat a spoon — if it pools, reduce another minute.

steps.title: Serve from the pot
steps.instruction: Fold in Parmesan off heat. Serve immediately — pasta waits for no one. Backup tray: cover lightly with foil at 200°F up to 15 minutes, add water if it tightens.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Baked Mac and Cheese with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Baked Mac and Cheese on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
